meta.title: fix!: Update publishObject to use json patches
meta.body_summary: Implement JSON Patch with string-append optimization for publishObject, reducing network traffic by sending incremental diffs instead of full objects, especially beneficial for streaming LLM output.

perf_labels.notes: Cursor authored initial JSON patch implementation with string ops; extensive bot and human review caught edge cases, leading to iterative fixes before merge.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 3493 changed lines, this is a large change by absolute volume, concentrated in the gensx-core package with a new feature. It fits a significant performance optimization that required multiple iterations to get right, but ultimately merged after thorough review.

review_details.concern_detail: cursor[bot] repeatedly flagged runtime errors in path traversal functions, including missing null checks, unsafe type casts, and incorrect root-level string-append behavior; human reviewers discussed removing string-diff operation and pause/resume behavior.
review_details.performance_claim: JSON patches reduce network traffic by sending only incremental changes instead of full objects, improving performance for streaming like LLM output.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Implementing JSON patch with custom string operations required precise handling of JSON Pointer path traversal, null types, and array indices; initial agent code contained multiple edge-case bugs, necessitating significant human fixes, indicating the agent struggled with complex type handling in this performance optimization.

detection_detail.code_reading: Human review by dereklegenzoff and EvanBoyle scrutinized string-diff risk and pause/resume behavior.
detection_detail.ci_auto: cursor[bot] performed automated code review, generating 13 review reports highlighting bugs like missing null checks, type mismatches, and root path failures.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No benchmark numbers or reproducible performance test; only narrative claim in PR body.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: jmoseley committed multiple fixes (16 commits) addressing edge cases flagged by bot reviews before merging.

core_change_summary.description: In gensx-core, publishObject now uses fast-json-patch to generate RFC 6902 JSON patches, sending incremental diffs instead of full objects. Custom string-append operation optimizes streaming string updates. The WorkflowObjectMessage format was changed to support patches. Auxiliary functions applyObjectPatches, getValueByJsonPath, and state clearing utilities were added. Numerous edge cases around null values, array paths, root paths, and non-string targets were fixed through iterative commits.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Linting fixes and unrelated file cleanups across many packages; main logic in gensx-core.
change_trajectory: Initial commit: Implement JSON patch for publishObject.
Add patch support in useObject hook and gensx-react.
Scope object state tracking to workflow context.
Remove string diff operation per review discussion.
Handle primitive and array values in publishObject.
Fix edge cases for invalid patches.

review_signals.summary: Flagged that applyObjectPatches fails when target path does not exist, has missing null checks, and mutates state incorrectly.
Reported that getValueByJsonPath/getValueByPath mishandle null and non-object values during path traversal.
Indicated that fast-json-patch compare is called with non-object types causing runtime errors.
Pointed out root path (/) breaks string-append because pathParts becomes empty array.
Warned that string-append replaces non-string values instead of being a no-op, and mutates input state.
Suggested that string-diff might introduce edge case risk and could be omitted in favor of string-append only.
review_signals.action_taken: jmoseley removed string-diff operation in later commit.

review_signals.summary: Asked how the new publishObject works across workflow pauses/resumes.
review_signals.action_taken: jmoseley explained the behavior and mentioned future checkpoint integration.

review_signals.summary: Approved PR with rocket emoji after fixes.

collaboration_trajectory: PR opened with initial JSON patch implementation by Cursor agent, co-authored by jmoseley.
cursor[bot] performed automated review within minutes, flagging multiple edge-case bugs.
jmoseley pushed a series of commits to address bot-reported issues, covering null checks, root paths, primitive handling, and array support.
Human reviewers engaged: dereklegenzoff questioned string-diff complexity; EvanBoyle asked about pause/resume semantics.
jmoseley removed string-diff per discussion and clarified resume behavior; after 16 commits and 5.3 hours, PR was approved and merged.
